title: Your first words
goal: A one-syllable word is one stroke: starting sounds, vowel, ending sounds.

blocks.x: Say it, split it, strike it

items: Say the word slowly; find the **vowel sound**.
Sounds after it: right-hand keys (lessons 5 and 6).

blocks.x: To find the vowel, say the word and **feel** where it opens the mouth. A word with no start or no end omits that hand ([[at|AT]], [[out|OUT]]).

blocks.title: Say it, split it, strike it
blocks.x: Five to start. Keys light up after a miss.
This is not a word list to memorise: it teaches **deriving** a stroke from a sound, the fallback for any unmemorised word.

If everything fits in steno order, it is one stroke. A word of two or more syllables usually needs more, built with the join key (lesson 10). Many common ones have a memorised one-stroke form (next lesson).
